security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates an Smcsps conditional stack swap instruction (c.sspush, c.sspopchk, m.sspush, m.sspopchk) without generating a runtime check that the source register (x2/sp) has its lower 4 bits zero (rs[3:0] == 0), causing the instruction to execute successfully with a misaligned stack pointer instead of raising an illegal instruction exception as required by the spec
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: trans_.*sspush|trans_.*sspopchk without preceding gen_helper_raise_exception for ILLEGAL_INST on (get_gpr.*x2|rs)[3:0] != 0
security_spec.summary: Missing x2[3:0]==0 trap on Smcsps conditional stack swap allows misaligned SP value bits to alias with PUSH/PPUSH metadata stored in msp/ssp CSR lower 4 bits, corrupting interrupt context swap control state

findings.finding: Smcsps is not implemented in this QEMU codebase. The sspush/sspopchk instructions in trans_rvzicfiss.c.inc are Zicfiss shadow-stack instructions that operate on the ssp CSR, not Smcsps conditional-stack-pointer-swap instructions that operate on x2/sp. No Smcsps opcodes (mcspspush/mcspspop/scspspush/scspspop) exist in any decode file, no mspcs/sspcs CSRs exist, and no ext_smcsps/ext_sscsps flags exist. The vulnerability pattern (missing lower-4-bit-zero check on x2/sp) does not apply.

spec_citations.excerpt: NOTE: As per the RISC-V psABI, stack pointers are at least 4 B aligned. Therefore, at least the two least significant bits of the stack pointer are zero in psABI compliant code.
mspcs.SP = tmp[XLEN-1:4]  /* save original value of sp into mspcs */ ... The spec masks off bits [3:0] but does not mandate an illegal-instruction exception for non-zero lower bits.

findings.finding: This is a Zicfiss shadow-stack-pop-check instruction, not an Smcsps instruction. It compares the shadow-stack top value against rs1 (x1/ra or x5/t0), not x2/sp. The MSB-zero check for x2/sp from the Smcsps spec does not apply. No vulnerability.
